name: Kalimpong Momo Shop
why_it_matters: The default momo stop on the single-street Lachen bazaar — most overland convoys headed for Gurudongmar pull in here for the 7am breakfast slot. Steamed not fried, dough hand-rolled in front of you, jhol-style chilli broth on request. Run by a Kalimpong-origin family who moved up to North Sikkim in the early 2000s.
insider_tip: Order before your driver leaves at 4am for Gurudongmar — they pack momos for the road in foil. The pork is fattier and warmer than the chicken at altitude.

name: Ingredient Resto-Bar
why_it_matters: One of two sit-down evening rooms in Lachen with table service after 7pm; the other is the in-house dining room at Magellan's. Local-cook menu plus the mainstream Indo-Chinese list that overland tour groups expect.
insider_tip: Heat is patchy after 9pm — eat by 8pm or take it back to your homestay. They'll pour a Hit beer if you ask, though it's not on the printed menu.

name: Magellan's The Grand Lachen — Restaurant
why_it_matters: The hotel dining room most overland operators use as their group-meal contract for Lachen. Buffet runs lunch and dinner during the Apr-Jun and Sep-Nov peak; à la carte off-season. The dining hall is one of the few rooms in Lachen with reliable heating after sunset.
insider_tip: Non-residents can eat here but should phone the front desk by 4pm — kitchen orders only what tour bookings demand. Skip the continental section; the Sikkimese add-ons (gundruk, churpi soup) are what's actually cooked fresh.
signature_address: Magellan's The Grand Lachen, Lachen, North Sikkim 737120

name: Hotel Kunzang Lachen — Dining
why_it_matters: Mid-range hotel kitchen that opens its set-menu dinners to non-residents in shoulder season. One of the few places in Lachen serving a proper hot dal-rice-vegetable plate at 7pm — important when most homestays stop cooking at 8.
insider_tip: If your homestay food is thin, walk in by 6:30pm and ask for the staff plate. Sikkimese-Indian set, ₹400-500 per head, no menu printed.

name: Lachung Heritage Bar & Restaurant (Singring)
why_it_matters: The closest thing Lachung has to a sit-down evening room with a printed Sikkimese menu — most other establishments are hotel kitchens or pure dhaba. Carries a beer-and-wine licence, which is rare in North Sikkim outside Gangtok.
insider_tip: Order the chhurpi (yak cheese) soup — Lachung's version uses harder, more aged cheese than Gangtok's. The phagshapa (pork-belly with radish) is on the printed menu but they cook it only when there's pork in from Chungthang.

name: The Yarlam Resort — Multi-Cuisine Restaurant
why_it_matters: The largest hotel dining room in Lachung and the default contract kitchen for most North Sikkim tour-package itineraries. Buffet lunch and dinner during Apr-Jun rhododendron season; reduced to set menu Nov-Feb.
insider_tip: Non-residents can eat dinner if they call the front desk before 3pm. The Sikkimese sides (chhurpi soup, gundruk) are quietly available on request — the printed buffet shows only the Indian-Chinese-Continental triangle.

name: Le Coxy Resort — Restaurant
why_it_matters: Older mid-range resort dining room overlooking the Lachung Chu river. Used heavily by Bengali tour groups headed to Yumthang, with kitchen oriented toward fish-friendly Bengali Indian rather than the heavier Tibetan-Sikkimese register.
insider_tip: Vegetarian thali is the safer bet — fish supply at this altitude is unreliable. Open garden seating works for an hour at midday; after 4pm the cold cuts dinner short.
signature_address: Le Coxy Resort, Lachung, North Sikkim 737120

name: Dun Khang Fast Food
why_it_matters: The cheapest hot meal on Lachung bazaar — momos, thukpa, packet Maggi with extra egg. Where drivers and porters eat between airport-runs from Yumthang.
insider_tip: Walk in before 11am; by 1pm the Yumthang day-tour buses arrive and the wait runs 30 minutes. Plates are aluminium, not ceramic — pack tissues.

name: Tsomgo Lake Food Court
why_it_matters: A clustered row of state-licensed food stalls on the shore-side, run as a local cooperative under the Sikkim Tourism framework. Open during lake-permitted days only; closed Monday-Tuesday when the lake permits do not run. Hot momos and thukpa at 12,000 ft are the actual draw — there is no other warm food for 40 km in either direction.
insider_tip: Cleanliness is uneven — pick the stall with visible turnover and steam coming off the momo basket, not the one with pre-cooked noodles in foil. Carry exact change; UPI does not work above the Tsomgo military checkpoint.

name: Lucky 7 Restaurant
why_it_matters: One of the named, semi-permanent eateries inside the Tsomgo cafeteria cluster — appears in trekker-blog references over multiple seasons rather than the seasonal pop-up rotation. Closes Mon-Tue with the lake permits.
insider_tip: Hot veg thali is the best altitude food here — heavy meat at 3,750m makes the descent harder. The dal-rice plate runs ₹150-200 and arrives faster than the menu.
signature_address: Tsomgo Lake cafeteria block, East Sikkim 737101

name: Dil Maya Homestay — Kitchen
why_it_matters: First-recorded homestay on the Zuluk Silk Route, founded in 2005 by Gopal Pradhan. The kitchen serves outside guests on prior request — a rarity in Zuluk where most homestay food stays for residents only. House dal-bhat-tarkari with the family's own pickles is the signature.
insider_tip: Phone ahead by mid-afternoon for dinner — there is no walk-in service. Vegetarian default; chicken or pork only if you ask 24 hours ahead. Cash only.

name: Zuluk Sojourn Homestay — Kitchen
why_it_matters: One of the larger Zuluk homestays whose kitchen takes outside-guest dinners on call — a fixed Sikkimese set, no menu. The room runs warm-stove evening service from October through March, when the Old Silk Route circuit is busiest.
insider_tip: Same rule as Dil Maya — book by phone before 3pm. The set is one round of dal-bhat-tarkari with the family's pickle and a clay-pot tea finish; do not expect refills.
